newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TONGAAT SEES GROWTH IN SUGAR, BUILDING.
newsitem.headline: TONGAAT SEES GROWTH IN SUGAR, BUILDING.

text.p: South African aluminium to foods group Tongaat-Hulett Ltd said on Wednesday that it aims to expand its sugar and building operations.
The firm, which earlier posted sparkling first half results and a bullish profit forecast, said that its sugar operations were hungry for downstream buys.
"The (sugar) division will continue to seek out profitable downstream investments in the future," managing director Cedric Savage told a news conference.
Tongaat already has a project in Mozambique seeking to help re-establish a sugar industry in the war-ravaged country and Savage said talks were taking place on setting up a second venture there.
Savage also said the firm's building unit had developed a strategic expansion plan and was waiting for an anticipated upturn in the construction industry in order to put it into practise.
"We have marginal expansion plans which are collectively significant, but we neeed the demand to justify the implementation of these plans," he said.
Earlier the firm posted a 32.8 percent increase in first half headline earnings per share to 200 cents and said that its full year earnings are expected to jump 30 percent.
The news pushed Tongaat's stock up more than two percent higher in late trade and the share 125 cents firmer to 58 rand -- the day's high -- with 50,700 shares having changed hands.
Shortly before the results were released the share was 75 cents off its opening levels.
